name: Salta, Jujuy and the North-West
tagline: A high, dry land of rainbow-coloured canyons, adobe villages, Andean traditions, salt flats and high-altitude vineyards, unlike the rest of Argentina.
highlight: The Hill of Seven Colours at Purmamarca, glowing at dawn above the adobe village and the market.
shortDescription: A colourful region of Salta's colonial centre, the canyons of Cafayate, the UNESCO-listed Quebrada de Humahuaca, Purmamarca's coloured hill, Salinas Grandes and the Train to the Clouds.
metaDescription: A Salta and Jujuy travel guide: Salta city, Cafayate and the Quebrada de las Conchas, Purmamarca and the Seven Colours Hill, Quebrada de Humahuaca, Salinas Grandes, Tren a las Nubes, altitude, best time and a five-day plan.
nearestAirport: Martín Miguel de Güemes, Salta (SLA); Jujuy (JUJ) is also served
knownFor: Colourful canyons, Andean culture, folk music, empanadas, Torrontés wine
goodFor: Landscapes, culture, road trips, wine, photography

image.alt: The multicoloured Hill of Seven Colours above the village of Purmamarca in Jujuy

intro: Argentina's north-west is a different country in feel from Buenos Aires or Patagonia. The region was part of the Inca Empire, and later a major route of Spanish colonial trade to the silver mines of Potosí, and its culture is strongly Andean, with Quechua and Aymara influences in language, food, music and clothing. Landscapes range from lush valleys and cloud forest to high desert and salt flats, and much of it lies above 2,000 metres.

Salta, the regional capital, is an elegant colonial city known as Salta la Linda, Salta the Beautiful, with a pink cathedral, a lively main square and excellent folk music venues, or peñas. From here, roads lead in two directions. South, the Calchaquí Valleys and Cafayate offer red canyons, adobe villages and some of the world's highest vineyards. North, in Jujuy Province, the Quebrada de Humahuaca, a UNESCO-listed valley, has villages such as Purmamarca and Tilcara, layered hills of red, pink and green, and pre-Inca ruins.

The region is best visited by road, with a hire car or a driver, since the sights are spread out and public transport is limited. Altitude is a factor, and the sun is strong. It is one of Argentina's most rewarding regions, with fewer visitors than Patagonia and a warm hospitality.

whyVisit.intro: The north-west offers landscapes and culture found nowhere else in Argentina.

points.title: Coloured mountains
points.text: Hills striped in red, orange, green and purple, at Purmamarca, Cafayate and elsewhere.

points.title: Andean culture
points.text: Weaving, folk music, markets and fiestas rooted in pre-Columbian tradition.

points.title: High-altitude wine
points.text: Torrontés and Malbec from vineyards in Cafayate at 1,700 metres.

points.title: Empanadas and regional food
points.text: Humitas, tamales, locro and llama, among Argentina's best regional cooking.

points.title: Epic road trips
points.text: Winding mountain passes, salt flats and desert landscapes.

attractionsIntro: Split your time between Salta, the southern valleys and the Quebrada de Humahuaca.

attractions.name: Salta city

image.alt: The pink neo-baroque cathedral on the main square of Salta

attractions.text: A colonial city with a pink cathedral, the Cabildo, lively squares and museums, including the Museum of High Altitude Archaeology. The cable car up Cerro San Bernardo gives a view of the valley.
attractions.tip: Spend an evening in a peña with live folk music.

attractions.name: Cafayate and the Quebrada de las Conchas

image.file: File:Quebrada de las Conchas, Comuna de Cafayate, provincia de Salta, Argentina.JPG
image.alt: The red rock formations of the Quebrada de las Conchas near Cafayate

attractions.text: A dramatic gorge of red rock, with formations such as the Devil's Throat and the Amphitheatre, on the road to Cafayate, a wine town in the valleys, known for Torrontés.
attractions.tip: Stop at viewpoints, and drive in the afternoon light.

attractions.name: Purmamarca and the Hill of Seven Colours
attractions.text: A small adobe village at the foot of a striped hill, with a craft market and a 3-km circuit path, the Paseo de los Colorados.
attractions.tip: Go at sunrise or sunset for the best colours.

attractions.name: Quebrada de Humahuaca

image.alt: The colonial town hall in Humahuaca on the plaza

attractions.text: A long valley inscribed by UNESCO in 2003, following an ancient route from the Andes to the plains, with villages such as Tilcara, Uquía and Humahuaca, and pre-Inca fortresses.
attractions.tip: Allow a full day or two.

attractions.name: Salinas Grandes

image.alt: The vast white Salinas Grandes salt flat under a blue sky

attractions.text: A vast white salt flat at about 3,450 metres, reached by the high Cuesta de Lipán road, where salt is still harvested by hand.

attractions.name: The Train to the Clouds

image.file: File:Tren a las nubes cruzando Viaducto la Polvorilla.jpg
image.alt: The Train to the Clouds crossing the La Polvorilla viaduct high in the Andes

attractions.text: A famous railway that climbs from Salta to the La Polvorilla viaduct, at over 4,000 metres. Services have been suspended at times, so check whether it is running.

thingsToDoIntro: Driving, walking and eating make up most of the days.

thingsToDo.title: Drive the Quebrada de las Conchas
thingsToDo.text: Stop at rock formations and viewpoints on the road to Cafayate.
thingsToDo.tip: Go in the morning or late afternoon.

thingsToDo.title: Taste Torrontés in Cafayate
thingsToDo.text: Visit bodegas, and try the aromatic white wine.
thingsToDo.tip: Book a tour with a driver.

thingsToDo.title: Walk around Purmamarca
thingsToDo.text: Follow the Paseo de los Colorados at the base of the hill.

thingsToDo.title: Visit Tilcara's pucará
thingsToDo.text: A restored pre-Inca fortress above the village.

thingsToDo.title: Go to a peña
thingsToDo.text: Live folk music, empanadas and wine in a small venue.

thingsToDo.title: Try coca leaves or tea
thingsToDo.text: The traditional remedy for altitude sickness.

foodIntro: The north-west's cuisine is Andean, with corn, potatoes, quinoa and spicy stews.

foods.name: Empanadas salteñas
foods.text: Small, juicy empanadas with beef, onion and spices, baked in clay ovens.

foods.name: Humitas and tamales
foods.text: Sweet or savoury corn dishes, wrapped in husks and steamed.

foods.name: Locro
foods.text: A thick stew of corn, beans and meat, eaten on national holidays.

foods.name: Llama and goat
foods.text: Lean Andean meats, grilled or stewed.

accommodation.intro: Stay in Salta, and in small guesthouses in Cafayate and Purmamarca.

areas.name: Salta city
areas.text: Hotels and hostels near the main plaza.

gettingThere.intro: Salta is about 1,500 km north-west of Buenos Aires, and reached by air.

options.text: Direct flights from Buenos Aires, about 2 hours.
options.detail: The airport is 15 minutes from the centre.

options.text: Long-distance buses run from Buenos Aires (about 20 hours) and Tucumán.
options.detail: Fly instead unless you love buses.

gettingAround.intro: A car or driver is the best way to explore, and tours cover the main sights.

options.text: Gives freedom, though roads can be unpaved and high.
Day trips from Salta and Jujuy.

bestTime.headline: April–October
bestTime.summary: The north-west has a dry winter and a rainy summer, with heavy afternoon storms from December to March. Altitude makes nights cold.

seasons.text: Dry, warm days, and clear light.
Dry and sunny, with cold nights.
Hot and wet, with afternoon storms and landslides.

bestTime.avoid: January and February, when rain can close roads.

itinerary.title: Five days in the north-west
itinerary.intro: Salta, the southern valleys and the Quebrada de Humahuaca.

days.title: Salta
days.morning: Arrive and see the plaza and cathedral.
days.afternoon: The cable car to San Bernardo.

days.title: To Cafayate
days.morning: Drive the Quebrada de las Conchas.
days.afternoon: Arrive in Cafayate and taste wine.

tipsIntro: The altitude and distances need some planning.
tips: Take it easy on arrival, since altitude can cause headaches and fatigue.
Drink plenty of water, and avoid alcohol on the first day at altitude.
Wear sun protection, since the UV is strong.
Bring layers, since nights are cold.
Fill your fuel tank often, and check road conditions.
Check whether the Train to the Clouds is running.
Try coca tea, and buy crafts from local cooperatives.

faq.q: How many days do you need in the north-west?
faq.a: Five to six days, including Salta, Cafayate and the Quebrada de Humahuaca.

faq.q: What is the best time to visit?

faq.a: It can be, particularly at Salinas Grandes and the high passes. Go slowly, drink water and rest.
It is the best way to explore, though tours are available.

faq.q: Is the Train to the Clouds running?
faq.a: Services have been suspended at times. Check the current status before planning.

faq.q: Which is better, Salta or Jujuy?
faq.a: They are complementary. Salta has the city and wine, and Jujuy has the Quebrada de Humahuaca.
